To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD151- and especially Tspan8- competent exosomes are essential for tumor cell metastasis by supporting matrix remodelling, reprogramming stroma and hematopoeitic cells and inducing EMT.
tumor exosomes promote tumor progression by supporting matrix degradation, reprogramming the microenvironment and by driving non-metastasis cells towards a motility phenotype.

tumor exosomes promote metastasis by supporting tumor-stroma crosstalk, which involves matrix remodelling and inflammatory cytokine expression, as well as tumor cell reprogramming towards a motile, metastatic phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exosome-mediated communication between cancer initiating cells (CIC) and their surrounding and highlights the importance of exosomal tetraspains for this process.
the role of tetraspanins in the communication between cancer initiating cells, tumor stroma and hematopoeitic cells, which may contribute to tumor progression.

the identification of tetraspanins as key exosomal components for the c-Met-driven tumor-stroma crosstalk in pancreatic adenocarcimomas and highlights the importance of tetraspanin-associated exosomes in metastasis promotion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tetraspanins in general and CD151 and Tspans in particular are important exosome-associated proteins that support the metastatic process.
CD151 and TSpan8 are essential for exosome formation and exosomes containing both tetraspanin proteins are required for the crosstak between tumor cells and their environment.
CD151-/Tspn8-competent tetraspanin-rich exosomes promote metastasis and that this is at least partly mediated by their ability to induce EMT in tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD151 and TSpan8 are crucial exosome components for tumor-stroma crosstalk, tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
tumor exosomes are essential for the crosstalking between tumor cells and their surrounding, which is at the basis of metastatic dissemination.
CD151 and TSpan8 cooperate to promote metastasis via exosomes and the crosstalk with the tumor microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tumor exosome targeting by metastasis-promoting CD151 and Tspans is essential for tumor cell dissemination.
tetraspanin-deficient tumor exosomes do not support metastasis and are thus promising candidates for tumor-targeted therapy.
CD151- and/ or Tspan8- deficient tumor exosomes are not only less effective, but may even be counteracting the metastatic potential.
